_comment: Catalog read by the `help` operation. One entry per dispatcher match arm in dispatcher.gd, shaped {summary, params, example, notes, see} plus an optional action_types for batch operations. `params` is the curated schema a caller should read: only the keys that operation uses, each described with (required) or (default: X) and the value shape, required keys first. `action_types` documents each entry of an `actions` array; a value of "@<op>" means "the params of that operation's entry, minus scene_path and save_path, which the batch owns". `help '{"op":"X","verbose":true}'` additionally prints the derived superset of keys the dispatcher accepts. Everything here is checked by `help '{"check_examples":true}'`: every params key, every action_types key and every example key is re-derived from the operation's own sources, so a renamed parameter fails that run instead of shipping a dead key. Add an entry in the same commit as the operation.

add_node.summary: Add one new node of a class under an existing node and save the scene.

params.scene_path: (required) scene to edit, project-relative or res:// — "scenes/main.tscn"
params.node_type: (required) class to instantiate: any instantiable engine class or project class_name — "Sprite2D", "CharacterBody2D", "VBoxContainer"
params.node_name: (required) name of the new node, and its path segment afterwards — "Player"
params.parent_node_path: (default: "root") path from the scene root, which is always addressed as "root" — "root/Panel"
params.index: (default: -1 = last) sibling position to insert at; for Control/CanvasItem siblings this is also draw order
params.properties: (default: {}) node properties by name, typed JSON — {"position": {"__type": "Vector2", "x": 160, "y": 96}, "text": "Start"}
params.groups_add: (default: []) group names to add the node to — ["actors"]
params.groups_remove: (default: []) group names to remove from the node

notes: Node paths start at the scene root, which is always addressed as "root" (or "."): "root/Panel/Start".
The scene must already exist; use create_scene or scene_batch with create_if_missing to make one.
More than one edit to the same scene belongs in scene_batch — it loads and saves the scene once and rolls back if any action fails.
The keys inside properties/indexed_properties/metadata are node property names, not parameters, and are never param-checked.

attach_script.summary: Assign an existing .gd script to a node and write its exported properties.

params.script_properties: (default: {}) values for the script's @export properties, typed JSON — {"speed": 220.0}
params.replace_existing: (default: true) false refuses to overwrite a different script already on the node

notes: The script must already exist and parse; a script with a parse error fails to load and the op errors instead of writing a half-wired scene.
script_properties only reach @export (or otherwise settable) properties declared by that script.
After adding a script with class_name, run `godot --headless --path <project> --import` before validating, or every other script referencing it fails to parse.

audit_imports.summary: Report the import state of every asset: ok, missing, invalid, stale, or orphaned.

params.include_entries: (default: true) false returns only the counts, without the per-file list

notes: Read-only. Run `python3 scripts/import/import_project.py <project>` first to actually (re)import, then audit.
Statuses are ok, missing, invalid, stale, and orphaned.

bake_collision.summary: Generate a StaticBody3D + CollisionShape3D under a MeshInstance3D from its mesh.

params.mode: (default: "trimesh") "trimesh" concave static-only, "convex" single hull, or "multi_convex" convex decomposition
params.clean: (default: true) convex only: remove duplicate/degenerate points before hulling
params.simplify: (default: false) convex only: simplify the hull
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the result to a different scene file

notes: node_path must point at a MeshInstance3D that already has a mesh.
trimesh collision is static only — a RigidBody3D needs convex or multi_convex.
Reruns replace the body this op generated instead of stacking a duplicate.
Also available as a scene_batch action.

bake_csg.summary: Freeze a CSGShape3D tree into a static ArrayMesh, optionally with collision, in place of the CSG nodes.

params.out_mesh: (no default) path to save the baked ArrayMesh — "meshes/level.res"
params.replace_with_meshinstance: (default: false) swap the CSG node for a MeshInstance3D holding the baked mesh
params.bake_collision: (default: false) with replace_with_meshinstance, also add a StaticBody3D/CollisionShape3D
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the rewritten scene elsewhere

notes: node_path must be the CSG root (is_root_shape) — a child CSG node has no baked geometry of its own.
Give at least one of out_mesh or replace_with_meshinstance; with neither there is nothing to produce and the op errors instead of reporting a silent success.
Without replace_with_meshinstance the scene is left untouched and only out_mesh is written.
CSG geometry updates one frame late, so this op runs inside the live SceneTree and awaits frames before baking.

build_animation.summary: Build an Animation from declarative value/method/bezier tracks and save it and/or register it on an AnimationPlayer.

params.tracks: (required) [{"type": "value"|"method"|"bezier", "path": "NodePath:property", "keys": [...]}]; value keys are {"time", "value", "transition"}, method keys {"time", "method", "args"}, bezier keys {"time", "value", "in_handle", "out_handle"}
params.scene_path: (no default) scene holding the AnimationPlayer to register the clip on
params.player_node_path: (default: "root/AnimationPlayer") the AnimationPlayer node, created when missing
params.create_player_if_missing: (default: true) false errors instead of adding the AnimationPlayer
params.library: (default: "") AnimationLibrary name; "" means the clip plays by bare name
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the edited scene elsewhere

notes: Track paths are Godot's "NodePath:property" form relative to the AnimationPlayer's root_node (its parent by default).
Value tracks also take update_mode (continuous/discrete/capture) and interpolation (nearest/linear/cubic).
The default library is "", so the clip plays by bare name: player.play("blink").
Give resource_save_path, or scene_path + player_node_path, or both — with neither the built animation is discarded.

build_animation_tree.summary: Build an AnimationNodeStateMachine on an AnimationTree from clips that already exist on the AnimationPlayer.

params.states: (required) [{"name": "run", "animation": "run", "position": {"x": 0, "y": 0}}]; animation defaults to name and must already exist on the AnimationPlayer
params.tree_node_path: (default: "root/AnimationTree") the AnimationTree node, created when missing
params.anim_player: (default: "../AnimationPlayer") NodePath to the AnimationPlayer, relative to the AnimationTree node
params.auto_start: (default: true) add a Start -> first state transition when none exists
params.create_tree_if_missing: (default: true) false errors instead of adding the AnimationTree node
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the edited scene elsewhere

notes: Each states[*].animation must already be registered on the linked AnimationPlayer (build_animation puts it there).
A Start -> first state transition is added unless one exists (auto_start: false disables) — without it the machine never enters a state.
Drive it at runtime with tree.get("parameters/playback").travel("run"); set conditions with tree.set("parameters/conditions/moving", true).
For blend trees or blend spaces, assemble tree_root with resource_batch call_method instead.

build_replication_config.summary: Author a SceneReplicationConfig .tres for a MultiplayerSynchronizer.

params.properties: (required) [{"path": ".:position", "spawn": true, "replication_mode": "never"|"always"|"on_change"}]; paths are "NodePath:property" relative to the synchronizer's root_path
params.create_if_missing: (default: true) false requires the resource to exist already

notes: Property paths are relative to the synchronizer's root_path (its parent by default).
Assign the result with configure_node's replication_config property on the MultiplayerSynchronizer.

build_sprite_frames.summary: Build SpriteFrames animations on an AnimatedSprite2D from a spritesheet grid or a list of frame files.

params.spritesheet: (atlas mode) the sheet texture to slice — "art/sheet.png"
params.animations: (atlas mode) [{"name", "fps", "loop", "frames": [...]}]; a frame is {"row","col"} / {"row","cols":[..]} / {"index"} / {"region":{"x","y","width","height"}} / {"path"}, each with an optional "duration"
params.frames_dir: (legacy mode) directory of frame images, sorted by name — "art/player_idle"
params.fps: (legacy mode, default: 10) frames per second for animation_name
params.loop: (legacy mode, default: true) whether animation_name loops
params.resource_save_path: (no default) also save the SpriteFrames standalone — "anims/mob_frames.tres"

notes: Two shapes: spritesheet + grid + animations (multiple clips, per-frame duration), or the legacy animation_name + frames_dir/frame_paths.
duration is SpriteFrames' relative per-frame duration (default 1.0), not seconds.
Import the spritesheet first (`godot --headless --path <project> --import`) or the saved resource will not reload later.

build_theme.summary: Author a Theme .tres grouped by control type: styleboxes, colors, constants, font sizes, and type variations.

params.types: (default: {}) {"<ControlClass>": {"styleboxes": {...}, "colors": {...}, "constants": {...}, "font_sizes": {...}, "fonts": {...}, "icons": {...}}} — item names must match the control's documented ones
params.default_font_size: (no default) int, the theme-wide default font size
params.default_base_scale: (no default) float, scales every theme constant (pixel-art UI often uses 1.0)
params.create_if_missing: (default: true) false requires the .tres to exist already

notes: Item names are not validated by the engine — a typo silently falls back to the default theme, so match the control's documented item names.
Author every interactive state (normal/hover/pressed/focus/disabled), not just normal; a missing focus stylebox makes keyboard/gamepad navigation invisible.
Styleboxes accept the flat shorthand above, an inline {"__resource_type":"StyleBox..."}, a {"__resource":"res://..."} reference, or the string "empty".
Wire the finished theme project-wide with project_batch set_setting on gui/theme/custom.

build_tileset.summary: Author a TileSet .tres: atlas sources, exposed tiles, physics/custom-data layers, terrains.

params.create_if_missing: (default: true) false requires the .tres to exist already

notes: Per-tile keys (on a tile entry or on sources[*].tile_defaults): collision ("full_cell" or 3+ {x,y} points), collision_layer_index, custom_data, terrain_set, terrain, peering.
Without collision polygons a TileSet is decorative and characters fall through — "collision": "full_cell" needs at least one physics_layers entry.
Run the importer first when the texture is a fresh unimported image, or the saved .tres will not reload in a later session.
paint_tilemap then assigns this TileSet to a TileMapLayer and paints cells.

check_project.summary: Load (and instantiate) every script, scene, shader, resource, GDExtension, and plugin, and report failures.

params.instantiate: (default: true) also PackedScene.instantiate() every scene; false is a load-only pass that runs no project code

notes: Run it with `--debug --ignore-error-breaks` on the godot command line, or no GDScript warnings are printed at all.
Pipe the combined output through scripts/debug/godot_log_parser.py for line-level diagnostics, or just use scripts/debug/validate_project.py which does both.
failed_count 0 is not a pass on its own: Godot degrades gracefully where the editor is fatal, so read the parsed diagnostics too.
instantiate is what catches broken node hierarchies; it runs each scene root's _init() and stored-property setters, so set it false only when that has side effects.

collision_from_sprite.summary: Trace a sprite's alpha silhouette into CollisionPolygon2D children, one per opaque island.

params.texture: (default: the node's own texture) image to trace — "art/enemy.png"
params.alpha_threshold: (default: 0.1) alpha above which a pixel counts as solid, 0.0-1.0
params.epsilon: (default: 2.0) outline simplification in pixels; lower means more vertices and more physics cost
params.one_way: (default: false) mark the generated colliders one-way (platform tops)
params.centered: (default: the sprite's own centered) offset points by half the texture size
params.offset: (no default) extra {"x", "y"} nudge applied to every point
params.collision_name: (default: "CollisionPolygon2D") base name for the generated children
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the edited scene elsewhere

notes: texture defaults to the target Sprite2D's own texture; pass it explicitly when the node has none yet.
The colliders are added under the sprite; give them a parent body (CharacterBody2D/StaticBody2D) for them to collide.
Reruns replace the colliders this op generated instead of stacking duplicates.

configure_control.summary: Set a Control's layout preset, anchors, offsets, size flags, minimum size, and theme overrides.

params.layout_preset: (no default) LayoutPreset name applied to anchors and offsets together — "FULL_RECT", "CENTER", "TOP_WIDE", "BOTTOM_WIDE"
params.anchors_preset: (no default) same preset names, anchors only
params.offsets_preset: (no default) same preset names, offsets only
params.position: (no default) {"__type": "Vector2", "x", "y"} — only meaningful outside a Container
params.custom_minimum_size: (no default) {"__type": "Vector2", "x", "y"}; the reliable way to size a control inside a Container
params.stretch_ratio: (no default) float share of the leftover space among EXPAND siblings

notes: Build the layout out of containers first. A bare Control does not place its children, so absolutely positioned siblings all resolve to (0, 0) and stack — the single most common broken-UI cause.
Inside a Container, position/size are overwritten by the parent every layout pass; use custom_minimum_size and the size flags instead.
Verify the result with a run_scenario ui_report step and fail_on, not by eye.

configure_node.summary: Set properties, indexed properties, groups, metadata, and unique_name_in_owner on an existing node.

params.properties: (default: {}) node properties by name, typed JSON — {"texture": {"__resource": "res://art/player.png"}, "z_index": 1}
params.unique_name_in_owner: (no default) true makes the node reachable as %Name in scripts

notes: This is the general property setter — prefer it over load_sprite for assigning a texture.
The keys inside properties/indexed_properties/metadata are project data and are never param-checked; a typo there fails at assignment time instead.
Use configure_control for Control layout: anchors, presets, size flags, and theme overrides.

connect_signal.summary: Connect a node's signal to a method on a target node, persisted in the scene file.

params.method_name: (required) method on the target, declared by its script — "_on_start_pressed"
params.binds: (default: []) extra arguments appended to the signal's own — ["clicked"]
params.persist: (default: true) store the connection in the .tscn (CONNECT_PERSIST)
params.deferred: (default: false) CONNECT_DEFERRED: call at idle time instead of immediately
params.one_shot: (default: false) CONNECT_ONE_SHOT: disconnect after the first emit
params.replace_existing: (default: true) false errors when the same connection already exists

notes: The target node needs a script that declares method_name, or the connection loads but fails at emit time.
inspect_scene lists the connections a scene already holds.
disconnect_signal removes it again by the same four fields.

create_scene.summary: Create and save a new scene with a typed root node.

params.root_node_name: (default: "root") name of the root node; later operations still address it as "root"

notes: Use scene_batch with create_if_missing for an idempotent create-or-open plus the first few nodes in one call.
root_node_type is any instantiable class name (Node2D, Control, Node3D, CharacterBody2D, ...).
The root is addressed as "root" by every later operation regardless of root_node_name.

disconnect_signal.summary: Remove a persistent scene connection by source node, signal, target node, and method.
notes: All four fields must match the stored connection exactly; inspect_scene lists the connections a scene actually holds.
Only connections stored in the scene are removed — connections made at runtime with .connect() live in code.

export_mesh_library.summary: Build a .meshlib MeshLibrary from a 3D scene's mesh children, for GridMap.

params.mesh_item_names: (default: [] = every mesh child) restrict the export to these child names — ["Floor", "Wall"]

notes: scene_path and output_path are both required; the op errors instead of exiting 0 when either is missing.
Feed the result to paint_gridmap as mesh_library; the item ids are the MeshLibrary indices.

get_uid.summary: Report a file's .uid sidecar path, whether it exists, and any engine-reported UID.
notes: Read-only diagnostic for projects that cross-reference resources by UID.
Headless-saved .tres/.tscn files carry no uid= header; run resave_resources to try to regenerate the sidecars, then re-check.

gltf_export.summary: Export a scene or a subtree to .glb/.gltf through GLTFDocument.

params.out: (required) output file; the extension picks the format (.glb binary, .gltf text). res://, user://, absolute, or project-relative

notes: The extension of out selects the format: .glb binary, .gltf text.
Import stays with the standard --import pipeline.

help.summary: List every dispatcher operation, or print one operation's parameters, example, and runnable command.

params.op: (no default; omit to list every operation) operation to describe — "add_node"
params.format: (default: "json") "text" renders the same information as plain lines
params.verbose: (default: false) with op, also print accepted_keys: the full derived key set the dispatcher will accept
params.check_examples: (default: false) validate every catalog params/example key against the keys its operation really reads; exits 1 on any failure

notes: help '{}' lists every operation with a one-line summary; help '{"op":"<name>"}' prints that one in full, including a command you can paste.
params is the curated schema: only the keys that operation uses, required first. verbose adds the derived superset the param check accepts.
The operation list is read out of dispatcher.gd's match arms and the accepted keys out of each op's source, so help can never describe an operation the dispatcher cannot run.

inspect_image.summary: Describe an image as text: size, blankness, opaque ratio, content bbox, dominant colors, optional ASCII art.

params.image_paths: (alternative to image_path) describe several images in one call — ["art/a.png", "art/b.png"]
params.ascii: (default: false) add an ASCII rendering by luminance, aspect-corrected
params.ascii_width: (default: 64) column count of the ASCII rendering
params.ascii_color: (default: false) add the nearest-colour grid (K W R G B Y C M per cell)
params.compare_to: (no default) second image to diff against; adds diff_ratio — "tests/reference/player.png"
params.max_unique: (default: 4096) cap on the exact unique-colour count
params.background_tolerance: (default: 0.12 for .jpg/.jpeg, else 0) per-channel colour distance, 0-1, under which a pixel still counts as background for content_bbox and quadrants; raise it for lossy WebP or noisy captures, 0 forces an exact match
params.expect: (no default) machine checks that fail the run, e.g. {"not_blank": true, "min_opaque_ratio": 0.1}
params.format: (default: "json") "text" prints the summary and any ASCII rows as plain lines

notes: Written for models that cannot see images: blank/opaque_ratio/content_bbox answer "did anything actually render" without looking at a screenshot.
ASCII rows are aspect-corrected because characters are about twice as tall as they are wide.
compare_to turns a visual regression into a number (diff_ratio) instead of a look.

inspect_project.summary: Report engine/host capabilities, selected settings, InputMap actions, autoloads, global classes, plugins, and export presets.

params.include_files: (default: false) also list every project file path; counts are always returned

notes: Start here on an unfamiliar project; include_files is usually noise.
Read-only. Autoload and InputMap names reported here are the ones project_batch edits.

inspect_resource.summary: Read a .tres/.res resource's stored values, dependencies, UID, and (for scripts) method/signal metadata.

params.include_schema: (default: false) add property type/usage metadata — enable only when you need to know what a property accepts
params.include_non_storage: (default: false) add properties the engine does not serialize
params.max_resource_depth: (default: 2) how deep nested sub-resources are expanded

notes: This is how to verify a resource_batch / build_theme / build_tileset write actually landed.
For a Script resource it also reports the methods, signals, and exported properties, which is how to check a method_name before connect_signal.

inspect_scene.summary: Read a scene's nodes, stored properties, connections, dependencies, and UID without instantiating it.

params.include_properties: (default: true) include each node's stored property values
params.max_resource_depth: (default: 2) how deep nested sub-resources are expanded

notes: Reads SceneState, so it runs no project code and never triggers a script's _init().
This is the only check that reveals a silently flattened hierarchy (every node parented to the root) — check_project and a clean boot both pass on one.
Reported node paths paste straight into a later node_path.

inspect_tilemap.summary: Dump a TileMapLayer or GridMap's painted cells as an ASCII map with a legend, bounds, and per-tile counts.

params.legend: (no default) force specific symbols, {"symbol": tile spec}; otherwise symbols are assigned automatically
params.bounds: (no default) restrict the dump to a rect, {"x", "y", "width", "height"} in cells
params.format: (default: "json") "text" prints the rows only, which is the readable form for a level layout

notes: Works on both TileMapLayer and GridMap; it is how to verify a paint_tilemap/paint_gridmap run without a screenshot.
The legend maps each ASCII character back to its source_id/atlas_coords (or mesh library item).
The rows it prints are the same shape paint_tilemap's ascii_map accepts, so a dump can be edited and painted back.

instantiate_scene.summary: Add an instance of another scene as a child node, optionally renamed and configured.

params.node_name: (default: the instanced scene's root name) rename the instance — "Enemy1"
params.index: (default: -1 = last) sibling position to insert at
params.unique_name_in_owner: (no default) true makes the instance reachable as %Name
params.properties: (default: {}) overrides applied to the instance's root node, typed JSON

notes: properties are stored as scene-instance overrides, so later edits to the instanced scene still flow through.
Reuse this instead of rebuilding the same subtree in every level scene.

load_sprite.summary: Load a texture resource into a Sprite2D, Sprite3D, or TextureRect (compatibility op).
notes: Kept for compatibility — configure_node with {"properties": {"texture": {"__resource": "res://art/player.png"}}} is the general form and works on any node with a texture property.
The texture must be imported already; a fresh PNG needs `godot --headless --path <project> --import` first.

paint_gridmap.summary: Assign a MeshLibrary and paint, fill, or erase cells on a GridMap node.

params.cell_size: (no default) {"__type": "Vector3", "x", "y", "z"} cell size in world units
params.clear: (default: false) erase every cell before painting
params.ascii_layers: (no default) [{"y": 0, "rows": ["###", "#.#"]}] painted through legend, one entry per height level
params.legend: (default: {}) symbol -> item spec for ascii_layers — {"#": {"item": 0}, ".": null}
params.erase_unlisted: (default: false) with ascii_layers, clear cells whose symbol is not in the legend
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the edited scene elsewhere

notes: item must exist in the mesh library (build it with export_mesh_library) — an unknown id is rejected, not silently skipped.
orient is a 0-23 orthogonal basis index; 0 is unrotated.
Order per call: mesh_library -> cell_size -> clear -> erase -> cells -> fills -> ascii_layers. Also runs as a scene_batch action.
ascii_layers + legend is the readable form: [{"y": 0, "rows": ["AAAA", "A..A"]}] with {"A": {"item": 0, "orientation": 0}, ".": null}; rows map to z, characters to x, one entry per y slab.
Verify the result as text with inspect_tilemap, which reads GridMaps too.

paint_tilemap.summary: Assign a TileSet and paint, fill, erase, or terrain-fill cells on a TileMapLayer node.

params.clear: (default: false) erase every cell before painting
params.ascii_map: (no default) {"legend": {"#": {"source_id": 0, "atlas_coords": {"x": 0, "y": 0}}, ".": null}, "rows": ["###", "#.#"], "origin": {"x": 0, "y": 0}, "erase_unlisted": false} — paint a level as text
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the edited scene elsewhere

notes: TileMap (the monolithic node) is deprecated since 4.3 — add TileMapLayer nodes instead.
Painting fails fast when the atlas source has not exposed the requested atlas_coords; expose tiles with build_tileset first.
Order per call: tile_set -> clear -> erase -> cells -> fills -> ascii_map -> terrain_fills.

ascii_map is the readable way to author a level: {"legend": {"#": {"source_id": 0, "atlas_coords": {"x": 0, "y": 0}}, ".": null}, "rows": ["#####", "#...#"], "origin": {"x": 0, "y": 0}}. Rows are top-to-bottom (y), characters left-to-right (x); an unknown character aborts the paint and leaves the scene untouched; "." and " " leave cells alone unless ascii_map.erase_unlisted is true. inspect_tilemap dumps the same shape back out.
terrain_fills needs terrain membership plus peering bits on the TileSet.

project_batch.summary: Transactional project.godot edits: settings, InputMap actions/events, autoloads, layer names, main scene, translations, shader globals.

params.actions: (required) ordered array; every entry is {"type": <one of action_types>} plus that type's keys
params.backup_path: (no default) snapshot project.godot here before saving — "project.godot.bak"

add_input_action.replace: (default: false) true clears the action's existing events first

add_input_event.action_name: (required) existing action to add the event to

remove_input_event.event_index: (required) zero-based index of the event to remove

notes: Every action is applied in memory and ProjectSettings.save() is called once at the end.
save() rewrites project.godot wholesale: comments are dropped and keys re-sorted. Rely on version control, or pass backup_path to snapshot it first.
Values equal to the engine default are omitted from project.godot by design — read them back with inspect_project, not by grepping the file.
Order matters: add_input_action before add_input_event for the same action.

remove_node.summary: Delete a node and its subtree from a scene.

params.node_path: (required) node to delete; its whole subtree goes with it — "root/Placeholder"

notes: Connections stored in the scene that referenced the removed node go away with it; connections from other scenes do not.
The scene root cannot be removed.

reorder_node.summary: Move a node to a different sibling index under the same parent.

params.index: (default: -1 = last) new sibling position, clamped to the valid range

notes: Sibling order is draw order for Control and CanvasItem nodes — later siblings draw on top.
Inside a BoxContainer/GridContainer it is also the layout order.

reparent_node.summary: Move a node (with its subtree) under a different parent.

params.node_path: (required) node to move, by its path before the move — "root/Player"
params.keep_global_transform: (default: true) preserve the on-screen position by rewriting the local transform
params.index: (default: -1 = last) sibling position under the new parent

notes: Ownership is re-applied to the scene root so the moved subtree still serializes.
node_path is the node's path before the move; later operations must use the new path.

resave_resources.summary: Resave scenes and script-like resources under a path, then report how many .uid sidecars were created versus still missing.
notes: Headless-saved .tres/.tscn files carry no uid= header; run this after bulk creation when the project cross-references by UID.
Read the created/still-missing counts instead of assuming every resave produced a UID.

resource_batch.summary: Transactional Resource authoring: load/create/duplicate, set properties and metadata, call builder methods, bake navmeshes, save once.

params.actions: (required) ordered array; every entry is {"type": <one of action_types>} plus that type's keys
params.create_if_missing: (default: false) create the resource when the file does not exist
params.resource_type: (default: "Resource") engine class to create with create_if_missing — "Curve2D", "StyleBoxFlat", "NavigationPolygon"
params.script: (no default) custom Resource script to attach instead of / alongside resource_type — "items/item_data.gd"
params.duplicate_from: (no default) deep-copy this resource instead of creating an empty one
params.duplicate_subresources: (default: true) with duplicate_from, also copy nested sub-resources
params.save_path: (default: same as resource_path) write the result elsewhere

set_metadata.metadata: (required) {name: typed JSON value} written with set_meta

call_method.method: (required) method that exists on the resource — "add_point"
call_method.expect_ok: (default: false) fail the transaction when an Error-returning method does not return OK

bake_navmesh.obstruction_outlines: (2D, default: []) [[[x,y], ...], ...] holes cut out of the walkable area
bake_navmesh.faces: (3D NavigationMesh) flat list of [x,y,z] triangle vertices, a multiple of 3
bake_navmesh.source_meshes: (3D, default: []) [{"mesh": "res://..."}] collision/procedural meshes to bake from

notes: The file is written only after every action succeeds, so a failed action leaves the old resource untouched.

Prefer set_properties (inspectable through inspect_resource) and keep call_method for builder-only APIs: Curve2D.add_point, Gradient.add_point, Theme.set_color, Animation.add_track, TileSet.add_source, SpriteFrames.add_animation.
bake_navmesh needs collision/procedural geometry — the headless renderer cannot read visual meshes back from the GPU. Set agent/cell parameters with a preceding set_properties.
Dedicated ops exist for the common resources: build_tileset, build_theme, build_animation, build_replication_config.

save_scene.summary: Load a scene and write it back, to the same path or to a new one.

params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the result here — "scenes/main_copy.tscn"
params.new_path: (compatibility alias for save_path) prefer save_path in new calls

notes: Use it to duplicate a scene, or to normalize a hand-edited .tscn through the engine's own serializer.
It re-serializes the whole file, so hand-written formatting and comments are not preserved.

scene_batch.summary: Run a sequence of scene actions against one scene in memory and save only if every action succeeded.

params.actions: (required) ordered array; every entry is {"type": <one of action_types>} plus that action's keys (its operation's keys minus scene_path/save_path)
params.create_if_missing: (default: false) create the scene when the file does not exist
params.root_node_name: (default: "root") root node name used when creating
params.save_path: (default: same as scene_path) write the result elsewhere

notes: This is the default entrypoint for scene work: the scene loads once, actions run in order, and nothing is written if any action fails.
An action takes its own operation's keys minus scene_path and save_path — the batch owns opening and saving the scene.
Every action entry is param-checked the same way the top-level object is, so a misspelled key inside actions[2] is reported as actions[2].<key>.
create_if_missing + root_node_type make it an idempotent create-or-open.

set_import_options.summary: Patch the [params] section of an asset's .import sidecar and invalidate the imported artifact.
notes: Follow with `python3 scripts/import/import_project.py <project>` (or `godot --headless --import`) — the op reports reimport_required: true and changes nothing until the importer runs.
WAV loop is edit/loop_mode and the importer enum is offset from the resource enum: 0 Detect, 1 Disabled, 2 Forward, 3 Ping-Pong, 4 Backward. Ogg/MP3 use the loop bool plus loop_offset seconds.
Whole-number values are written as ints — JSON numbers arrive as floats and importer params are typed.
The keys inside options are importer parameter names and are never param-checked; audit_imports reports whether the reimport landed.

setup_audio_buses.summary: Create or update the project's audio buses, sends, volumes, and effects, then save and register the layout.
notes: Order buses before the buses that send to them; the Master bus cannot have a send.
Providing effects replaces that bus's whole effect chain, which keeps reruns idempotent.
Values equal to the engine default are omitted from project.godot by design.
Route a player to a bus with configure_node: {"properties": {"bus": "Music"}} on an AudioStreamPlayer.
